criteria.note: A versioned decision-review artifact (schema warp.decision_review/v1) is defined in .warp/decision_review.py, homed per-repo under .warp/decision_reviews/*.yaml, a subdirectory the single-level .warp/*.yaml engine glob does not sweep. I confirmed no .warp/decision_reviews/ directory ships anywhere (root, plugin/templates, packs) and a fresh init_scaffold lays no such directory. A review binds to a decision (a decision id + the decision_version reviewed) and captures the attack: problem_class_challenge (verdict + finding), a non-empty option_challenges list (each option + dead_end_verdict + finding), a required missing_options list (may be empty), a non-empty assumption_challenges list (each assumption + verdict + finding), a recommendation, and a disposition. The illustrative example ships at .warp/examples/decision-review-example.yaml reviewing the shipped draft decision-example (DEC-0000); I ran python3 .warp/validate.py decision-review .warp/examples/decision-review-example.yaml -> rc 0 and check_decision_review(example, decisions_dir=examples) -> 0. I verified the example names DEC-0000 and carries no chosen/decided_by (a review informs, never decides). The check is gate-wired via run_all's examples block.

validate_review (invoked by validate.py check_decision_review) structurally checks a review the way decision.py checks a record and fails closed BY NAME on each claimed class, which I reproduced independently over the real example and over fixture text: wrong schema id; missing/empty required field (id, decision, reviewer, recommendation) - I proved 'missing or empty required field: decision' and '...: recommendation'; non-integer version and decision_version ('a decision review is versioned' / 'a review binds to the exact decision version it reviewed'); out-of-vocabulary disposition ('must be one of [defensible, reframe, refuted]'), problem-class verdict, dead_end_verdict, and assumption verdict; an option_challenge or assumption_challenge lacking its finding; an empty option_challenges or assumption_challenges list ('a review that challenges nothing is not a review'); a duplicate option/assumption reference; a review that smuggles a decision (chosen, decided_by, decided_at) refused 'a decision review informs the human and never decides (O4, NG2)'; and a file outside the parser subset (tab indentation) surfaced as DecisionReviewError -> fail closed. decision_review.py imports only 're' and 'from pathlib import Path' and receives parse_yamlish, fail, and the decision loader from validate.py, so there is no second YAML parser and no import cycle. The well-formed review validates clean (rc 0), so the check is non-vacuous.

bind_review pairs a review to the decision it reviews and fails closed when the record is malformed or absent ('referenced but absent, fail closed'), when decision_version does not match the record's current version ('a stale review does not vouch for the current framing'), when the option_challenges do not COVER every option the decision declares ('option ... is not challenged: an adversarial review must attack every option'), when they reference an option the decision does not declare ('referenced but absent'), and symmetrically for assumptions. resolve_decision reads each record through the injected decision.load_record and matches on schema warp.decision/v1 and id, so a review-shaped file in the tree is never mistaken for a decision. I proved every direction over the real example decision (DEC-0000): version mismatch RED; drop an option challenge RED (partial attack); reference a ghost option RED; drop an assumption challenge RED; and the positive - the shipped example binds clean to the shipped example decision (rc 0).

The fresh-context adversarial reviewer is a DELEGATED seam that FAILS LOUD, mirroring executor.LiveLoop.review and dispatch.LiveReviewer (I read all three; the pattern and the message shape match exactly). AdversarialReviewer.review is the seam and raises NotImplementedError; the reference LiveAdversarialReviewer is wired to nothing and raises DecisionReviewError ('...no reviewer is wired. Inject a reviewer that dispatches a genuinely fresh context... Refusing to fabricate a review.'), which I invoked directly and confirmed. DecisionReviewError is a ValueError (raised by name). CRITICAL CHECK - no fabrication in code: I grepped the module for any assignment or return that could synthesize a review's disposition, verdict, recommendation, or findings; the ONLY occurrence is 'disposition = data.get("disposition")', which READS the value from the parsed artifact for a membership check, never synthesizes it. The module never constructs a review dict and never returns one. The .review() seam is not invoked anywhere in the engine or any gate path (the only call site is the selftest proving it raises); the module purely parses, validates, binds, and gates artifacts a real fresh context produced. A review can only enter through an injected reviewer or a parsed artifact - never fabricated.

decided_requires_review over the decision records refuses a record whose status is decided unless it carries at least required_reviews_for(risk) bound, valid adversarial reviews, read from .warp/policy.yaml risk_tiers (the single source of truth; standard=1, high=1, critical=2 verified live, and an absent tier or file defaults to 1, never 0). A review counts for a decision only when validate_review == 0 AND bind_review == 0, so a malformed, stale, or partial review cannot satisfy the gate. I proved over temporary trees (this repository's real policy.yaml copied in): no .warp/decisions/ directory stands the gate down (rc 0, adoption safe); a decided high record with ZERO bound reviews is refused; with one bound review passes; a decided critical/irreversible record with ONE review is refused with the exact message 'requires 2 ... scrutiny scales with reversal cost, D5'; with TWO distinct-id bound reviews passes; a stale-version review does not count; a decided low record needs one; and a DRAFT decision is not gated (the gate does not bite before a human decides). Adoption safe and fail closed both confirmed.

findings.text: HONESTY (NG5) - CORRECT boundary, no over-attestation. The builder ships the artifact format, its structural validator, the cross-artifact binding, the fail-loud delegated reviewer seam, the decided-requires-review gate, and a clearly-marked ILLUSTRATIVE example that reviews the DRAFT decision-example (DEC-0000). It did NOT manufacture a real adversarial verdict and did NOT flip the shipped decision example to decided - which is exactly right, because a real review must come from a genuinely fresh context, and fabricating one (or recording a human as having decided on the strength of a fabricated review) would be a false attestation. I confirmed no review's disposition/recommendation/findings are synthesized in code, that the reference reviewer fails loud, and that the capabilities entry (adversarial_decision_review, status: mechanical, home .warp/decision_review.py) is accurate: the validation, binding, and gate ARE mechanical and enforced today (I reproduced their teeth), while the entry and the module docstring both name the adversarial attack as a delegated fresh-context step and defer the in-session tripwire monitoring to WARP-1107. Nothing is marked mechanizable that nothing enforces.

NON-BLOCKING (the count-based scrutiny gate is structural, not semantic). decided_requires_review counts DISTINCT, valid, bound review IDs. I verified that two reviews with the SAME id are refused ('duplicate decision review id ... across reviews'), but two reviews with DIFFERENT ids and otherwise byte-identical content DO satisfy a critical decision's two-review requirement. This is not a defect: the structural gate cannot verify that two reviews came from genuinely INDEPENDENT fresh contexts (or a different reviewing model) - that independence is the same delegated/process boundary the reviewer seam itself embodies, and it is a founder instruction recorded in policy.yaml (L2, a fresh-context different Claude model), enforced by process, not by this validator. It fails CLOSED on count, never open, and the module never claims to verify independence content. Worth stating so the operator knows the gate proves 'N bound valid reviews exist', not 'N genuinely independent attacks were performed'.

NON-BLOCKING (clean separation, noted for completeness). In the standalone check_reviews path, decided_requires_review skips a decision record that fails to parse ('except Exception: continue', with the comment that a malformed record is reported by decision.check_decisions_dir). This is correct single-responsibility: the integrated gate (run_all) calls check_decisions() BEFORE check_decision_reviews(), so a malformed decided record IS caught by the record validator, and resolve_decision independently declines to count reviews bound to an unparseable record. No decided record can pass unreviewed through the integrated gate. I confirmed run_all's ordering (check_decisions then check_decision_reviews).

ENVIRONMENTAL PARITY (non-blocking, general to WARP commits). The 'generated' gate check is green because specs/index.md was regenerated at this commit; a rerun on a later day would flip it RED until the index is restamped (the same date-stamp behavior recorded in prior WARP reviews). summary: WARP-1106 (adversarial decision review - the warp.decision_review/v1 artifact, its structural validator and cross-artifact binding, the delegated fail-loud fresh-context reviewer seam, and the decided-requires-review gate; W6 of PLAN-0011) PASSES WITH NOTES at 9f15c8f with ZERO blocking findings. The code under review is identical to HEAD (575f854 adds only the manifest). AC1: a versioned per-repo review artifact under .warp/decision_reviews/ (unswept by the engine glob, shipped nowhere) binds to a decision and captures a problem-class, per-option, missing-option, and per-assumption attack plus a recommendation and disposition; the shipped example validates and binds clean and carries no decision. AC2: validate_review fails closed BY NAME on every claimed class (wrong schema, missing field, non-integer version/decision_version, out-of-vocab disposition/verdicts, a challenge missing its finding, an empty challenge list, a duplicate reference, a smuggled decision, a malformed file), reuses parse_yamlish + fail (no second parser, no import cycle), and passes a well-formed review. AC3: bind_review fails closed on an absent/malformed decision, a version mismatch, and incomplete-or-unknown option/assumption coverage; the example binds clean to DEC-0000. AC4: the reviewer is a delegated seam - LiveAdversarialReviewer raises DecisionReviewError, the base raises NotImplementedError, nothing in the module synthesizes a disposition/recommendation/finding (the sole match is a read of the parsed artifact), and the seam is never invoked in any gate path, so a review is never fabricated in code. AC5: decided_requires_review refuses a decided record with fewer than its tier's bound valid reviews (standard 1, critical/irreversible 2 per D5, read from policy.yaml risk_tiers), a draft is not gated, and absent dirs stand down - proven over temp trees. AC6: TEETH reproduced by me over the REAL example (strip a finding RED; remove the recommendation RED) and over a temp tree (delete the sole bound review RED; critical with one review RED 'requires 2'), each reverted byte-identical; 15 unclaimed mutations all fail closed and 4 over-refusal guards pass; the extended engine is byte-identical across all 8 copies; the init scaffold lays decision_review.py; the capability is honestly mechanical. RISK-TIER: standard is HONEST - the footprint touches only the single 'contracts' area (only validate.py maps; the new module is unarea'd like decision.py), footprint_tier_floor is empty and placement_gate is clean, so it is not a mistagged boundary crossing. Gate GREEN (selftest 1626/0; contracts, generated, docs, template sync, pack drift, runner catalog, secret scan all pass). RULE #1 clean, no protected path touched, manifest bound to 9f15c8f, proof_digest recomputes to sha256:c5323bb443ac8ea6. Four non-blocking notes: (1) the honest human-decides / delegated-attack boundary; (2) the gate counts distinct bound reviews but cannot verify semantic independence (a delegated/process property, fails closed on count); (3) malformed-record reporting is delegated to check_decisions in the integrated gate (clean separation); (4) standard index date-stamp environmental parity. Verdict: pass_with_notes.
